observations: E07 uses a bent forward swing knee and a side-on shoe pointing right; shin and ankle remain connected.

E08-v2 lowers the forward left boot relative to rejected E08-v1. Against E07, the shoe is near-level and remains above the following landing; the conspicuous rise in v1 is removed. Small canvas/body offset means this is a visual transition observation, not an exact shoe-pixel descent measurement.

The rear anatomical right leg remains the low support through E08, then the left foot becomes support in E09. No opposite-direction toe turn, knee inversion, disconnected ankle or both-feet-airborne pose identified.
E15 draws the forward anatomical right shin down into a compact bent-knee pose while the shoe continues pointing right.
E16 extends the forward leg toward the next touchdown without the earlier stiff outward kick silhouette. The rear left support remains visibly lower until the following right-foot landing in E01.
The wrap retains right sword and left talisman; no shoe reversal or new hand ownership error identified.
W13/14 move the forward anatomical left boot through compact bent-knee poses with a legible left-facing heel-to-toe axis. The previous strongly extended, raised-toe kick is reduced.
W15/16 extend that leg toward landing while keeping the shoe largely side-on toward the left; the ankle follows the shin rather than twisting away from it.
Rear anatomical right support remains low through W16; W01 changes to the forward left support with the other leg folding back.

Normal small shoe-pitch and silhouette changes remain, including limited underside visibility; none is a hard outward-twist defect. Upper-body cloth/hair variations remain but no material new pose-ownership discontinuity is identified.
Both complete 16-frame contact sheets were independently viewed under the latest straight-foot criterion, without relying on old pass flags.
NW08/16 and NE07/08/15/16 retain believable diagonal/rear-view knee-shin-ankle relationships. Visible dark blue sole areas are consistent with rear swing knee flexion and heel lift/push-off.

No hard foot reversal, ankle inversion, or sudden sideways shoe yaw is identified in this review. Do not flatten these into frontal legs or remove normal sole exposure merely to make every outline parallel.

constraints.timingTarget: 16 distinct frames, 75 ms each, 1200 ms cycle; this review does not retime anything.
constraints.sameFootStance: Preserve existing eight consecutive support poses and two distinct poses per relative foot position.
constraints.handAssignment: Anatomical right sword / anatomical left blue talisman.

limitations: This approval is for visual axis/pose continuity of the exact listed revisions and inspected boundaries, not actual client runtime testing or user acceptance.
Static sequences and adjacent-image comparison were used in this review; no new measured real-time playback test is claimed.
Cutout art has no world-space floor. Grounded appearance is assessed from weight-bearing pose and relative foot contact, not guaranteed world-space no-slip.
Original video has small character pixels and nameplate/effect/shadow occlusion, so it supports motion-plane comparison rather than exact per-frame toe-yaw measurements.
